description: Exported CO2 counts as storage of the capturing country (decision 20): it leaves the national captured-CO2 buffer and never enters an atmosphere; not counted against the national injection cap (research_co2_storage_cap); limitation: one ASEAN-wide unit cost, no transport from inland nodes to a port (LA is landlocked; its exports would need a corridor through a neighbour), offshore unloading facilities not in the IEAGHG 2004 scope

Cross-check: GCCSI 2025 Table 3 lists IEAGHG 2004 as the only published shipping cost beyond 2,000 km (US$10-44/t, 200-12,000 km); later studies at <= 2,000 km report US$9-50/t (IEAGHG 2020: 41-44 US$/t at 1,000 km and 1.4-1.8 Mt/a), i.e. the 2004 basis (large ships, 6.2 Mt/a) is at the low end
source: GCCSI (2025); IEAGHG (2020-10); IEAGHG (2025-08); ERIA (2022) Vol. II Table 2.8

description: Offshore storage, saline aquifer without legacy wells, ZEP 2011 Figure 19 Medium (Low 6 / High 20); DOGF alternatives 3/10/14 (no legacy wells), 2/6/9 (legacy wells)

Liquefaction (100 bar inlet) + ships + harbour + buffer tanks + loading/unloading at 4500 km, linear between the IEAGHG 2004 Table 5-3 values 3,000 km (17.34) and 6,000 km (24.92); 6.205 Mt/a, capital charge 11.02 %/a (10 %, 25 a)

Decision 89: unit cost of exporting captured CO2 to an extra-ASEAN offshore sink = liquefaction (CO2 at 100 bar) + ship transport (4500 km, midpoint of 3,000-6,000 km, IEAGHG 2004 Table 5-3, 50,000 t ships) + offshore saline-aquifer storage (ZEP 2011 Figure 19, Medium); 21.13 US$2004/t x 1.1690 + 14.0 EUR2009/t x 1.1467
source: IEAGHG (2004) Ship Transport of CO2, PH4/30; ZEP (2011) The Costs of CO2 Capture, Transport and Storage
